title: Deterministic connectivity verification and staged rollback SLOs for Private/VPC deploys
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define deterministic connectivity and upgrade acceptance criteria that allow private/VPC customers to verify network posture and safely perform operator-driven upgrades with no- or constrained-egress, and to execute a staged rollback when an upgrade or network partition causes service regressions.

Scope:
- Networking verification harness that can assert reachability between control-plane, operator, and node-level agents under: normal, partitioned, and delayed-egress conditions.
- Upgrade orchestration acceptance criteria with explicit rollback gates and SLOs (time-to-rollback, user-impact threshold, automated vs manual rollback decisions).
- Air-gapped constraints: offline artifact signing, deterministic image manifest validation, optional physical-media fallback instructions.

Out of scope:
- Full implementation of operator automation (ENG to own execution), hardware procurement for customer sites, and integrations with third-party on-prem proxies (these will be tracked separately).

Assumptions:
- Customers provide a minimal outbound allowlist when full zero-egress is not achievable (we support both zero-egress and minimal-egress modes).
- Operator has RBAC to trigger staged rollouts and rollbacks.
- We can deliver a local verification binary (lighter-weight than full operator) that can run during preflight.

Success metrics:
- Deterministic connectivity verification run completes in <10 minutes for a standard 3-control + 10-worker site and reports an explicit pass/fail with logged evidence.
- Upgrade canary stage failure detection and rollback execution completes within configured SLO (default: 15 minutes from detection to rollback start; rollback complete within 25 minutes).
- No silent failures: every failed upgrade that leads to rollback must produce an audit log and a dashboard entry with tokenized customer identifiers for postmortem correlation.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight connectivity verifier (CLI) is included in the private operator bundle and can be executed offline; output is a deterministic JSON manifest that includes: DNS resolution matrix, TCP/UDP connectivity matrix, MTU checks, and optional proxy handshake logs.

Operator upgrade flow exposes canary groups with configurable size (default 5%) and health checks; if canary health falls below threshold (default 99% of expected RPCs), automated rollback initiates per policy and emits a rollback-start event to audit logs.

All images and artifacts used for upgrades are signed with a customer- or Redwood-provided key; the operator verifies signatures offline using a cached public keyring and fails upgrade if signature validation cannot be completed deterministically.

A staged rollback path is defined with three phases: canary rollback (subset), regional rollback (site-level), and global rollback (all nodes); each phase includes explicit pre- and post-checks, and a maximum allowed duration to reach stabilization before proceeding to broader rollback.

Upgrade orchestration supports two network modes: zero-egress and minimal-egress; acceptance tests must pass for both modes in a lab harness. Minimal-egress mode documents the minimal allowlist endpoints and IP ranges required.

Deterministic connectivity verification includes simulation scenarios: asymmetric partition, delayed egress (packet delay jitter), operator-heartbeat loss, and inter-region routing change; tests must produce reproducible pass/fail results and a remediation suggestion for each failure type.

Operational observability: upgrade and rollback events are emitted to the customer's telemetry sink (syslog/Fluentd) and to Redwood Console telemetry when connected; sample dashboards and a curated alert rule set are delivered with the PRD.

Security: KMS rotation during offline upgrades is supported via a documented offline-wrap/unwrap flow; acceptance requires a documented test that simulates key rotation and validates artifact decryption post-rotation.

Customer-facing runbook: a single-page checklist for operators (preflight -> canary -> monitor -> rollback) is written, reviewed by support, and linked in the operator bundle; acceptance requires at least two internal runbook reviews and one customer pilot sign-off.
testing_plan: Lab harness: create an automated pipeline that deploys a 3-control + 10-worker private cluster into an isolated test VPC and runs the connectivity verifier in zero-egress and minimal-egress modes.
Chaos matrix: run controlled network experiments using tc/netem to introduce packet loss, reordering, and delay during upgrades to validate canary detection and rollback timing against SLOs.
Signature offline verification test: provision a test keyring, sign a curated set of operator artifacts, verify operator can validate signatures when the control plane has no external connectivity.

Timed rollback drill: trigger a canary failure, measure time from failure detection to rollback start and from start to cluster stabilization; verify it meets default SLOs and document tail-latency cases.
Customer pilot: run the preflight verifier and a staged canary upgrade with two pilot customers in different regions and collect feedback on operator ergonomics and runbook clarity.
notes: Trade-offs: Conservative detection thresholds reduce false positives but increase blast radius when a rollout is paused; default thresholds are opinionated but configurable per customer.

Design decision: Deliver both a lightweight verifier (CLI) for preflight and the full operator checks; CLI reduces friction for air-gapped customers who cannot run workloads on the cluster during onboarding.
Dependency: This PRD relies on an ENG deliverable to expose operator hooks for external verifier to fetch heartbeats and health metrics (tracked in ENG-1842).
Fallback: For customers that require physical-media upgrades, provide a signed-manifest workflow and a checksum reconciliation tool included with the operator bundle.
